title: Suarez: one act can adore prototype in the image via representative presence
source_text: L. At vero contra plurimi Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores in ea sunt sententia, imaginem adorari posse & debere eadem adoratione cum exemplari, ita ut imago propter prototypum, & prototypum in imagine adoretur uno eodemque actu, cujus objectum adaequatum sint exemplar & imago simul. Hanc sententiam prolixe tuetur & explicat Franciscus Suarez, tomo primo in tertiam Thomae, disputatione quinquagesima quarta jam saepe memorata. Ubi, ut clarius mentem suam exponat, observat imaginem, quamvis in se revera non contineat prototypum, secundum proprium esse reale illius, continere tamen in esse repraesentativo: Unde fit ut homo, proposita hujusmodi imagine, ipsum exemplar apprehendat, ac si revera in illa adesset, & per modum unius utrumque simul concipiat: ea igitur posita apprehensione, animum adorantis, uno adorationis motu, primario in exemplar, concomitanter vero in imaginem ferri, quam deosculando Christum ipsum adorat; non per deceptionem, quia non judicat imaginem esse Christum, sed per simplicem ac vivam repraesentationem exemplaris in imagine, ac si adesset.
pass_a_gloss: But on the contrary very many Doctors of the Roman Church are of this opinion, that the image can and ought to be adored with the same adoration as the exemplar, so that the image on account of the prototype, and the prototype in the image, is adored by one and the same act, whose adequate object are exemplar and image together. This opinion Franciscus Suarez prolixly defends and explains, in the first tome on the third part of Thomas, in disputation fifty-fourth so often already mentioned. Where, that he may set forth his mind more clearly, he observes that the image, although in itself it does not really contain the prototype according to the prototype's proper real being, yet contains it in representative being: Whence it comes about that a man, such an image being set before him, apprehends the exemplar itself as if it were really present in it, and conceives both together after the manner of one: that apprehension being posited, the mind of the adorant is carried by one motion of adoration primarily into the exemplar, but concomitantly into the image, which by kissing he adores Christ himself; not through deception, because he does not judge the image to be Christ, but through a simple and living representation of the exemplar in the image, as if it were present.
pass_b_english: Majority Roman line (Suarez): one act can adore image-for-prototype and prototype-in-image together as adequate object.
The image does not really contain the prototype, but contains it in representative being—so the mind takes both as one without mistaking paint for Christ.

choices.why: Secondary termination on the image in one act.
